title: Lombardia Diesel Reverses Course, Wiping Out Three Weeks of Gains
dek: Benzina keeps its slow, steady climb in Italy's most populous region, while Gasolio suddenly gives back a month of increases.
body: Lombardia's self-service Benzina sits at €1.9988/L today, just a fraction of a cent under the national self-service average of €2.0012/L — essentially matching the rest of the country. Gasolio is the more interesting number: at €2.0834/L self-service, it's now about a cent cheaper than the national average of €2.0938/L, a gap that only opened up in the last couple of days.

Zoom out over the past ten days and the two fuels have gone in opposite directions. Benzina has inched upward almost every day, from €1.9513 on July 21 to €1.9988 today, a slow but consistent 4.75-cent climb. Gasolio followed the same upward path through July 27, topping out at €2.2071 — then abruptly reversed, shedding more than 12 cents per liter in three days to land at €2.0834 by July 30. The region's station network held steady through it all: 3,117 stations registered, 2,863 reporting today, a reporting rate close to 92%, slightly above the national figure of roughly 91%.

A move like that — one region quietly unwinding a month of diesel increases in three days — is exactly the kind of detail a once-a-week spreadsheet update would miss entirely. Fuel Dashboard catches it because it rebuilds itself from the national MIMIT feed every single day, with no manual re-pulling of data. It's a small system built with Claude Code specifically so this level of daily, per-region tracking doesn't depend on anyone remembering to refresh a file.

caption:
Today's Fuel Dashboard spotlight: Lombardia, where self-service diesel just reversed a full month of gains — dropping over 12 cents a liter in three days — while gasoline kept its slow, steady climb toward the national average.

Fuel Dashboard tracks daily fuel prices across all of Italy's regions, pulling directly from the official MIMIT feed and rotating a regional spotlight every day. No manual spreadsheet, no stale numbers — just today's real figures, every day. Take a look: https://adeo-blip.github.io/fuel-price-italy/

What I like most about this project: the entire thing, from data pipeline to daily regional articles, was built with Claude Code instead of a manually maintained Excel file. It's a good example of what AI coding tools are actually good for right now — not just writing code faster, but building small systems that stay current on their own, so nobody has to remember to update anything.
